c1-m1.summary: Assistant suggests setting boundaries for managing time better.
c1-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hi, I'm looking for some new TV shows to watch. Can you give me some recommendations?
Assistant: I'd be happy to help you find some new shows to watch. What kind of genre are you in the mood for? Drama, comedy, or something else?
User: Hmm, I think I'd like to watch something with a good storyline and character development. Maybe something romantic?
Assistant: That sounds great! Romance is a popular genre. Are you open to watching shows from other countries, or do you prefer something from Hollywood?
User: Actually, I've been interested in watching shows from other countries lately. I've heard great things about them.
Assistant: There are many amazing shows from around the world. Let me ask, have you ever watched any Asian dramas before?
User: Yeah, I think I've seen a few episodes here and there, but I've never really followed a whole series.
Assistant: Asian dramas can be very addictive once you get into them. Which country's dramas are you most interested in? Japan, Korea, or maybe China?
User: I think I'd like to try a Korean drama. I've heard they're really popular.
Assistant: K-dramas are definitely a favorite among many drama fans. They're known for their catchy storylines, memorable characters, and addictive soundtracks.
User: That sounds great. I think I'd really enjoy that. You know, I've actually met someone recently who's a huge K-drama lover.
Assistant: Really? That's awesome! K-drama fans are always excited to share their favorite shows with others. What's this person like? Are they trying to get you into K-dramas too?
User: Yeah, they're really passionate about it. They've been recommending shows left and right, but I don't know where to start.
Assistant: I can imagine! It can be overwhelming with so many great shows out there. Let me help you narrow it down. What kind of themes or storylines is this person into? Are they more into rom-coms, melodramas, or historical dramas?
User: I think they like a mix of everything, but mostly rom-coms and melodramas.
Assistant: Okay, I think I have a good idea. I can recommend some popular K-dramas that fit those genres. Would you like me to suggest a few shows to get you started?
User: Hi, I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed lately. I was hoping to talk to someone about it.
Assistant: Of course, I'm here to listen! Can you tell me a bit more about what's been going on and how you've been feeling?
User: It's just that my schedule has been getting really full, and I'm not sure how to manage it all. I feel like I'm constantly running from one thing to another.
Assistant: That sounds really stressful. Have you taken on any new responsibilities or commitments recently that might be contributing to your busy schedule?
User: Well, I have been trying to get more involved in my community, which is great, but it's also taking up a lot of my time. I'm not sure if it's worth it.
Assistant: Getting involved in your community can be really rewarding, but it's also important to make sure you're not overcommitting yourself. What kind of community activities have you been doing?
User: I've been volunteering at a local charity, and I also joined a community club that aligns with my interests. It's been great to meet new people, but like I said, it's taking up a lot of time.
Assistant: Those sound like great activities, but I can see how they could be time-consuming. Have you noticed any benefits from being more involved in your community, or is it just feeling overwhelming right now?
User: Actually, I think being more involved in the community has increased my social commitments. I've been invited to more events and gatherings, which is nice, but it's also adding to my stress levels.
Assistant: That makes sense. It sounds like your involvement in local community events or volunteer work has increased your social commitments, which can be both positive and negative. On the one hand, it's great that you're meeting new people and feeling more connected to your community. On the other hand, it's understandable that you're feeling overwhelmed.
User: Exactly! I feel like I'm losing some of my free time and flexibility, which is important to me. Do you have any suggestions for how I can manage my time better and still stay involved in the community?
Assistant: One idea might be to set some boundaries for yourself, such as limiting the number of events you attend each week or month. You could also try prioritizing your commitments and focusing on the ones that are most important to you.
User: That's a great idea. I think I need to take a step back and evaluate what's working for me and what's not. Maybe I can find ways to be more involved in the community that don't require so much of my time.
Assistant: That sounds like a great plan. Remember that it's okay to say no to commitments that don't feel sustainable or enjoyable to you. Your well-being and happiness are important, too!

c3-m1.summary: The user enjoys watching K-dramas and is looking for diverse entertainment.
c3-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hey, I've been getting into K-dramas lately. Have you seen any good ones?
Assistant: Ah, I'm familiar with the genre. I can suggest some popular ones if you'd like. What kind of storylines are you into? Romance, thriller, or something else?
User: I love a good romance, but I'm open to other genres as well. What are some of your top picks?
Assistant: Well, for romance, you can't go wrong with "Crash Landing on You" or "Goblin". If you're in the mood for something a bit darker, "Stranger" is a great thriller. But I have to ask, what draws you to K-dramas?
User: I think it's the way they balance humor and drama. The storylines are always so engaging, and the characters are well-developed. Plus, I love learning about Korean culture through the shows.
Assistant: That's a great point! K-dramas are known for their ability to balance tone and genre. And they're a great way to learn about Korean culture, food, and traditions. Have you ever tried reading any Korean comics or webtoons?
User: Actually, I have! I stumbled upon a webtoon platform, and I've been reading a few series. It's been a great way to pass the time, especially when I need a break from watching shows.
Assistant: Ah, nice! Webtoons are a great way to consume Korean content, and they're often adapted into dramas or films. Do you find that reading webtoons helps you relax or is it more of a way to stay engaged with the stories you love?
User: It's a bit of both, I think. I love that I can take breaks whenever I need to without losing my place in the story. As a fan of K-dramas, I find that reading webtoons or manhwa allows me to do just that – take breaks whenever I need to without losing my place in the story.
Assistant: That makes sense. Webtoons are often designed to be easily digestible, with each episode being relatively short. And because they're visual, it's easy to pick up where you left off. Do you find that you prefer reading webtoons that are also K-drama adaptations, or do you like discovering new stories?
User: Hmm, that's a good question. I think I like a mix of both. It's fun to see how the webtoon compares to the drama, but I also love discovering new stories and characters. Speaking of which, do you have any webtoon recommendations?
Assistant: I can definitely suggest some popular ones. If you like romance, "Cheese in the Trap" is a great one. If you're in the mood for something a bit darker, "Omniscient Reader" is a great choice. And if you want something a bit more light-hearted, "Tower of God" is a great fantasy adventure series.
User: Awesome, thanks for the recs! I'll definitely check them out. And thanks for chatting with me about K-dramas and webtoons – it's been a lot of fun!
Assistant: No problem, happy to chat with you! It's always great to meet someone who shares similar interests. If you need any more recs or just want to discuss K-dramas and webtoons, feel free to reach out anytime!
User: Hey, I'm looking for something new to watch. Do you have any recommendations?
Assistant: Ah, what kind of shows are you into? Are you a fan of any particular genre or actors?
User: I love watching K-dramas! I've already seen all the popular ones, though. I'm looking for something different.
Assistant: That's great! K-dramas are so much fun. Have you considered checking out variety shows featuring your favorite K-drama stars? They're a great way to see them in a different light.
User: Actually, I haven't. I didn't know they existed. What kind of variety shows are there?
Assistant: There are tons! From game shows to cooking shows, and even travel shows. They're usually really fun and light-hearted. Plus, they're episodic, so you can easily jump in and out.
User: That sounds amazing! I love watching shows that I can easily pause and resume whenever I want. I have a pretty busy schedule.
Assistant: Exactly! Variety shows are perfect for that. And since they're not as plot-driven as dramas, you don't have to worry about missing out on important storylines if you miss an episode.
User: I can spend hours watching variety shows featuring my favorite K-drama stars, and since they're episodic, I can easily pause and resume whenever I want.
Assistant: Ah, I knew you'd be hooked! Variety shows can be so addictive. Do you have a favorite K-drama star that you'd love to see in a variety show?
User: Oh, yeah! I love Park Seo-joon. I've seen him in a few dramas, but I've never seen him in a variety show before.
Assistant: Ah, he's a great choice! Park Seo-joon is actually a pretty popular variety show guest. I think he's been on a few episodes of "Running Man" and "Knowing Bros". You should totally check those out!
User: Awesome, thanks for the rec! I'll definitely add those to my watchlist.
Assistant: No problem! I hope you enjoy them. And if you're looking for more variety shows, just let me know and I can give you some more recommendations.
User: Sounds good, thanks! I'm excited to start watching some variety shows.
Assistant: Yay! I'm excited for you! Variety shows are a whole new world of K-entertainment. Enjoy your watch!

I can understand why you were impressed by Laurence Fishburne's performance. Is there anything specific you would like to discuss about the movie?

The performances by Jack Lemmon and Sissy Spacek are outstanding. It's a gripping film that will keep you engaged. Here's a review I found: "[OTHER_HIS_LIKES_REVIEW_3]:Missing VHS:{'overall': 5, 'Review_text': 'I loved this film from beginning to end for so many reasons. One is the superb performances by Sissy Spacek and Jack Lemmon. 2. The story is so emotion provoking, maddening, saddening, and true. 3. Gravas' direction is great and he perfectly captures the atmosphere of Chile after the fascist Pinochet coup (backed by the USA). 4. The theme music by Vangelis is great atmospheric haunting very appropriate background. 5. Anyone who doesn't know much about the effects of US foreign policy must see this film to learn the truth.'}"
User: Oh, I've already seen "Missing" before. It was a great film. Do you have any other recommendations?
Assistant: I understand. Since you've already seen "Missing," I recommend checking out "Country Strong." User: Hey, I've been really into TV shows lately. I've been binge-watching so many series, but I've realized I'm missing out on a lot of international content. Have you got any recommendations?
Assistant: Ah, international content, huh? There's so much great stuff out there. I think you might enjoy some Korean dramas. They've been getting super popular worldwide. What genre are you into?
User: Hmm, I'm not picky, really. As long as it's engaging, I'll give it a shot. But I've heard great things about K-dramas. I've tried watching a few with subtitles, but I feel like I'm missing out on some nuances.
Assistant: That's totally understandable. Subtitles can only convey so much. If you want to truly appreciate the shows, learning some Korean would definitely help. Have you considered taking language classes?
User: Actually, I've been thinking about it, but I'm not sure where to start. Do you think it's worth the effort?
Assistant: Absolutely! Not only will you be able to enjoy K-dramas without subtitles, but you'll also gain a deeper understanding of the culture. Plus, learning a new language is a great way to challenge yourself and keep your brain active.
User: That sounds amazing. I've recently started taking Korean language classes to better appreciate K-dramas without subtitles. But I'm a total beginner, and I'm struggling to keep up with the pace. Do you have any tips for a newbie like me?
Assistant: Congratulations on taking the first step! I'm happy to help. One tip I can give you is to practice consistently, even if it's just for a few minutes each day. Try listening to K-pop songs or watching Korean variety shows with English subtitles to get a feel for the sounds and rhythms of the language.
User: That's a great idea! I love K-pop, so that's definitely something I can do. What about reading and writing? Should I focus on that too?
Assistant: Reading and writing are essential skills to master, but for now, focus on listening and speaking. Once you get more comfortable with the sounds and grammar, you can start practicing reading and writing. There are many online resources and language learning apps that can help you with that.
User: Okay, got it. So, what's the most challenging part of learning Korean for a beginner like me?
Assistant: One of the biggest challenges is probably the grammar and sentence structure. Korean grammar is very different from English, so it can take some time to get used to. But don't worry, with practice and patience, you'll get the hang of it. Another challenge is the pronunciation – Korean has some sounds that don't exist in English, so it can be tricky to get them right.
User: Yeah, I've noticed that already. But I'm determined to improve. Can you tell me a funny story about someone who learned Korean and had a hilarious experience?
Assistant: Ah, I've got one! A friend of mine learned Korean and went to Seoul for vacation. She was so proud of herself for being able to order food in Korean, but she accidentally ordered a super spicy dish thinking it was mild. Let's just say she had a very... memorable experience!
User: Oh no, that's hilarious! I hope I don't have a similar experience, but it's good to know that even with mistakes, I can still have fun with the language. Thanks for the chat, I feel more motivated to keep practicing now!
User: Hey, I'm thinking of trying some new recipes this weekend. Do you have any recommendations?
Assistant: That sounds like a great plan! I'd be happy to help. What kind of cuisine are you in the mood for? Italian, Mexican, or something else?
User: Hmm, I'm not sure yet. I've been feeling a bit adventurous lately, so maybe something a bit more exotic.
Assistant: Exotic sounds exciting! Have you considered trying any Asian recipes? There's a world of flavors to explore, from spicy Korean dishes to delicate Japanese desserts.
User: Actually, I've always been fascinated by Korean food. I've tried some Korean BBQ and loved it, but I've never ventured beyond that.
Assistant: Korean BBQ is a great starting point! If you're looking to try something new, I'd recommend exploring their street food scene. You could try making some kimchi or hotteok (Korean-style pancakes).
User: Kimchi? I've heard of that before, but I've never tried making it myself. Is it difficult to make?
Assistant: Not at all! Kimchi is actually quite easy to make, and there are many variations to try. It's a traditional Korean side dish made from fermented vegetables, usually cabbage or radishes, seasoned with spices and chili peppers.
User: That sounds interesting. I think I'd like to give it a try. Do you have a simple recipe to get me started?
Assistant: I can definitely provide you with a basic recipe. But before I do, I have to ask: are you prepared for the fermentation process? Kimchi can be quite... pungent.
User: (laughs) I think I can handle it. My favorite hobby is trying out new Korean recipes, especially kimchi variations. I've just been looking for some inspiration to take it to the next level.
Assistant: Ah, I had no idea! Well, in that case, let's get started with a recipe for a classic kimchi variation: baechu kimchi (cabbage kimchi). I'll walk you through the steps, and you can experiment with different seasonings and ingredients to create your own unique flavor.
User: Sounds like a plan! What's the first step in making baechu kimchi?
Assistant: First, you'll need to prepare the cabbage. Rinse it thoroughly, and then cut it into 2-inch pieces. Next, you'll need to create a brine solution to soak the cabbage in. This will help to soften the leaves and remove any impurities.
User: Okay, got it. What's the ratio of water to salt for the brine solution?
Assistant: For a traditional kimchi brine, you'll want to use a ratio of 1 cup of coarse salt to 5 cups of water. You can adjust this to taste, but this is a good starting point.
User: Alright, I think I'm ready to give it a try. Thanks for the guidance and inspiration!
Assistant: My pleasure! I hope your kimchi turns out delicious, and I'm always here if you have any more questions or need further assistance. Happy cooking!

User: Here is a piece of text: The Guam Visitors Bureau (GVB) is proud to announce that over 5,000 people attended the MBC Music K-Pop Concert on Guam at Governor Joseph F. Flores Memorial (Ypao Beach) Park on December 1. As the largest K-Pop concert to ever be held in the region, the event was filmed as a made-for-tv special by Korea’s top entertainment network, Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation (MBC). The concert will air as a 90-minute special in winter 2018 with over 23 million viewers anticipated to watch on MBC’s networks throughout the world. The concert featured global K-Pop sensation Twice, as well as Supernova, JBJ95, Mighty Mouth, and H.U.B. Local groups Inetnon Gefpå’go and Skip Entertainment kicked off the free concert with their award-winning performances. Of the thousands in attendance, 74% were local residents and 26% were international visitors. Preliminary numbers show that 3,417 concert-goers were Guam residents, in addition to 467 Korea residents, 382 Japan residents, 226 U.S. Residents, 115 Philippines residents, 89 Greater China residents, and 17 Russia residents. Additionally, the Guam Police Department, Guam Fire Department, Visitor Safety Officers and members of the private sector worked together with GVB to keep the event grounds safe for concert-goers. The event also had a variety of vendors for food, drinks, merchandise, and other products. It also provided family-friendly activities, such as face painting, and featured a visiting delegation from Boryeong, South Korea that promoted their city’s annual mud festival. The MBC Music K-Pop Concert on Guam was presented by Lotte Duty Free, along with other sponsors including Bank of Guam, IT&E, Grid Corporation, The Guam Daily Post, Pepsi Guam, ABC stores, Foody’s Guam, The Westin Resort Guam, and Modetour. Special thanks is given to South Pacific Petroleum Corporation, Nault Tech, Med Farm, Royal Bics, CNMI Office of the Governor, Guam Music Inc., Gil Shinohara, Guam Premier Outlets, Tumon Sands Plaza, JCT Rental, NetTours, Japan Bus Lines, T Galleria by DFS, Happy Idea Company, Officer of the Governor and Lt. c37-m2.summary: As the largest K-Pop concert to ever be held in the region, the event was filmed as a made-for-tv special by Korea’s top entertainment network, Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation (MBC).
c37-m2.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Here is a piece of text: The Guam Visitors Bureau (GVB) is proud to announce that over 5,000 people attended the MBC Music K-Pop Concert on Guam at Governor Joseph F. Flores Memorial (Ypao Beach) Park on December 1. As the largest K-Pop concert to ever be held in the region, the event was filmed as a made-for-tv special by Korea’s top entertainment network, Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation (MBC). The concert will air as a 90-minute special in winter 2018 with over 23 million viewers anticipated to watch on MBC’s networks throughout the world. The concert featured global K-Pop sensation Twice, as well as Supernova, JBJ95, Mighty Mouth, and H.U.B. Local groups Inetnon Gefpå’go and Skip Entertainment kicked off the free concert with their award-winning performances. Of the thousands in attendance, 74% were local residents and 26% were international visitors. Preliminary numbers show that 3,417 concert-goers were Guam residents, in addition to 467 Korea residents, 382 Japan residents, 226 U.S. Residents, 115 Philippines residents, 89 Greater China residents, and 17 Russia residents. Additionally, the Guam Police Department, Guam Fire Department, Visitor Safety Officers and members of the private sector worked together with GVB to keep the event grounds safe for concert-goers. The event also had a variety of vendors for food, drinks, merchandise, and other products. It also provided family-friendly activities, such as face painting, and featured a visiting delegation from Boryeong, South Korea that promoted their city’s annual mud festival. The MBC Music K-Pop Concert on Guam was presented by Lotte Duty Free, along with other sponsors including Bank of Guam, IT&E, Grid Corporation, The Guam Daily Post, Pepsi Guam, ABC stores, Foody’s Guam, The Westin Resort Guam, and Modetour. Special thanks is given to South Pacific Petroleum Corporation, Nault Tech, Med Farm, Royal Bics, CNMI Office of the Governor, Guam Music Inc., Gil Shinohara, Guam Premier Outlets, Tumon Sands Plaza, JCT Rental, NetTours, Japan Bus Lines, T Galleria by DFS, Happy Idea Company, Officer of the Governor and Lt. Governor, and Department of Parks and Recreation. User: Here is a piece of text: The Guam Visitors Bureau (GVB) is proud to announce that over 5,000 people attended the MBC Music K-Pop Concert on Guam at Governor Joseph F. Flores Memorial (Ypao Beach) Park on December 1. As the largest K-Pop concert to ever be held in the region, the event was filmed as a made-for-tv special by Korea’s top entertainment network, Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation (MBC). The concert will air as a 90-minute special in winter 2018 with over 23 million viewers anticipated to watch on MBC’s networks throughout the world. The concert featured global K-Pop sensation Twice, as well as Supernova, JBJ95, Mighty Mouth, and H.U.B. Local groups Inetnon Gefpå’go and Skip Entertainment kicked off the free concert with their award-winning performances. Of the thousands in attendance, 74% were local residents and 26% were international visitors. Preliminary numbers show that 3,417 concert-goers were Guam residents, in addition to 467 Korea residents, 382 Japan residents, 226 U.S. Residents, 115 Philippines residents, 89 Greater China residents, and 17 Russia residents. Additionally, the Guam Police Department, Guam Fire Department, Visitor Safety Officers and members of the private sector worked together with GVB to keep the event grounds safe for concert-goers. The event also had a variety of vendors for food, drinks, merchandise, and other products. It also provided family-friendly activities, such as face painting, and featured a visiting delegation from Boryeong, South Korea that promoted their city’s annual mud festival. The MBC Music K-Pop Concert on Guam was presented by Lotte Duty Free, along with other sponsors including Bank of Guam, IT&E, Grid Corporation, The Guam Daily Post, Pepsi Guam, ABC stores, Foody’s Guam, The Westin Resort Guam, and Modetour. Special thanks is given to South Pacific Petroleum Corporation, Nault Tech, Med Farm, Royal Bics, CNMI Office of the Governor, Guam Music Inc., Gil Shinohara, Guam Premier Outlets, Tumon Sands Plaza, JCT Rental, NetTours, Japan Bus Lines, T Galleria by DFS, Happy Idea Company, Officer of the Governor and Lt. Governor, and Department of Parks and Recreation. User: Given the text: These days, it’s incredibly common to see sports teams wearing special uniforms to commemorate causes, holidays and events, and we recently wrote about NFL teams utilizing special colors to raise awareness for causes. One of the more popular uniform tweaks across multiple sports leagues is camouflage-patterned uniforms to pay tribute to the armed forces. So where did this trend start?
It’s difficult to pinpoint exactly when the light switch turned on and teams began wearing special camo uniforms to honor the military, but most would credit the San Diego Padres with beginning the trend. Home to a large port for the U.S. Navy, San Diego has long been proud of its naval tradition. It only made sense for the Padres to tip their cap to the U.S. Navy, and they’ve done so with regularity ever since introducing a camo uniform in 2000. The uniforms have undergone several variations, including desert storm tan, navy blue, and classic green. The camouflage pattern has also changed with the military’s shift to digital camouflage, which utilizes small squares instead of the more organic shapes found on camo in decades past. Several other baseball teams have begun including camouflage alternate uniforms, such as the Pittsburgh Pirates.
For having the most liberal use of camouflage on their team’s uniforms, MLB uses it the most infrequently of any major sports league. College and high school sports are where the real camo game lies. With Veteran's Day this weekend, we’ve compiled a few our of favorite ones from over the years.
Kansas State University – Not one to sideline their bright purple color scheme, the wildcats used a purple digital camo pattern on their existing helmet design to pay tribute to the military.
University of Southern Mississippi – You won’t find yellow and black camo on the battlefield, but you will find it on the football field. Here’s another case of a team keeping their color scheme while adding a camo element.
University of Oregon & Georgetown University – How about a 2-for-1 usage of camouflage? The Fighting Ducks sidelined their usual yellow in favor of gray and white camo while the Hoyas implemented a navy blue camo that mostly matches their existing color scheme.
University of Oregon – Back in 2013, the Oregon Ducks football team wore a uniform that was predominantly olive drab, complete with the backwards-facing U.S. Flags on their right sleeves. It may not be camo, but it’ll do for our purposes.
While not every team has worn full-fledge camouflage uniforms, there’s plenty of uniform tweaks and accents throughout the last decade. Which one has been your favorite? Do you like the camouflage look or wish teams would stick to more traditional designs? Let us know in the comments below!
Can you provide examples of college and high school sports teams that have incorporated camo patterns into their uniforms to pay tribute to the military?
Assistant: - Kansas State University
- University of Southern Mississippi
- University of Oregon
- Georgetown University

Assistant: I am unable to share images or links. However, you can easily search for images of these camo uniforms on the internet using the team names mentioned in the article.

Assistant: The article doesn't provide a comprehensive list, but it does mention that camo-patterned uniforms to pay tribute to the armed forces are common across multiple sports leagues. The article specifically talks about college and high school sports incorporating camo patterns into their uniforms. In addition to baseball, some examples of other sports that have utilized camo uniforms to honor the military include football, basketball, and hockey.

Germany was the first team to win by more than one goal, against Ukraine.
Mykhailo Fomenko's team was the first at the EURO 2016 championship to lose by two goals. Did Ukraine deserve to lose by two goals against Germany tonight? No way. Fomenko has created an organized side, showing good physical preparation, very good teamwork. Ukraine played some brave, solid soccer. Unfortunately, being brave and passing the ball around the pitch is not enough against a German team which purrs like a well-oiled Mercedes Benz, which works 24 hours a day for 25 years without stopping and without a breakdown...without conceding a goal.
Germany does not miss a pass and from beginning to end launches constant attacks on both flanks, in the center, on the ground, on the volley and in the air. Guardiola's passage in Bayern Munich also gave the German midfield the quality of tiki-taka, the short-passing game which is so difficult to play against.
Nobody can deny that Poland deserved the win, although Northern Ireland showed spirit, graft and courage, organization and teamwork, witness of the reason why the team has reached the final phase of the EURO 2016 championship in France.
Poland had 18 shots against Northern Ireland's 2, 8 corners to 1 and a ball possession of 60 per cent against 40. This superiority however was not translated into goals and throughout the game, Northern Ireland looked as if the slender lead could be cut. It was not to be.

Today, Albania, Wales and Iceland are participating as equals in the final phase of major championships. We saw why today. Wales got three points, Albania lost but was not outclassed.
Russia faced a young England team fired up by the cultured coach, Roy Hodgson. England today can pass the ball, can close the gaps at the back, can score and park the bus. Russia until today could not compete on equal terms with the world's best, except on rare occasions. Passes went astray, shots went wide...many Russians said "Soccer and Russia do not mix". Today, Russia re-wrote its footballing history.
Leonid Slutski's team fought on equal terms with an excellent and young England squad. Did Russia deserve to win the game? Frankly, no. But it would not have been a scandal if Russia did. Did Russia deserve to lose the game? Frankly, no. Conclusion: the result was fair.
England attacked more but the Russian defense was resolute throughout. And more, the Russian team respected England but was never over-awed.

Slovakia saw one come back off the woodwork, saw 4 magnificent saves, had more ball possession, but Wales weathered the storm, held on and came back to clinch the winner. A magnificent team effort, proof that Wales is more than Gareth Bale. Chris Coleman substituted Williams for the goal-scorer: for Ján Kozák's side, Duda came on after 60 minutes and scored almost immediately.
At the Stade de France, in Paris, Didier Deschamps' France, the hosts, faced Anghel Iordanescu's Romania. The teams had drawn four of their last five competitive matches and at the EURO, the last two encounters ended in a 1-0 win for Framce in 1996 and a 0-0 draw in 2008.
Iordanescu had said before the match started that he aimed to qualify for the next round and also to show quality football. And he delivered. At half-time, Romania had had an equal chance of a goal and had been denied a clear penalty.
The first situation of danger came on 4' after a corner to Romania, the ball was cleared off the French line by goalkeeper Lloris. On 10', Griezmann came back for France, getting a corner from which Giroud headed just wide. Giroud took advantage of a rebound on 14', firing against the post. On 36', Griezmann fired just wide as once again France created danger.
38 minutes, PENALTY TO ROMANIA!!
But not given by the referee Viktor Kassai. And one was clearly fouled in the penalty area, receiving a treacherous and dangerous kick to his knee.
The first half ended with Giroud heading over from a corner. Chances for both sides, France ahead in terms of attack, but Romania resolute.
After the break, Stanciu fired wide after gaining a good position on 48' but France came back. Tatarusanu saved on the line on 52', and again on 57' denied Pogba. On 58', Giroud back-headed the first French goal from outside the area.
Romania did not give up and on 64', Stanciu was fouled in the area, and scored (65') from the resulting penalty. 1-1. End-to-end stuff until right at the end of the game, when Payet pulled off perhaps the goal of the tournament in the first match, firing into the top right-hand corner from outside the area. Space given by the Romanian defence, but a spectacular piece of timely individual skill.

c89-m1.summary: The 80s were a period of significant fashion innovation and diverse design.
c89-m1.source_conv_dialogue:
User: Hi, I'm interested in learning about 80s fashion. Can you tell me about some popular designers of that era?
Assistant: The 80s was a fascinating time for fashion, with many iconic designers emerging during this period. Some notable designers include Giorgio Armani, Versace, and Jean Paul Gaultier. They were all influential in shaping the decade's fashion trends.
User: That's really interesting. Were there any American designers who made a significant impact during that time?
Assistant: Yes, there were several American designers who made a significant impact in the 80s. Some notable ones include Ralph Lauren, Calvin Klein, and Stephen Sprouse. They each brought their unique style and aesthetic to the fashion world.
User: I think I've heard of Stephen Sprouse before. What was his style like?
Assistant: Stephen Sprouse was known for his bold and edgy designs, often incorporating graffiti and punk rock elements into his work. He was particularly famous for his Day-Glo-colored clothing and his collaboration with the artist Andy Warhol.
User: That sounds like a really unique style. Did he have a significant following?
Assistant: Yes, Stephen Sprouse had a dedicated following, especially among the downtown New York City crowd in the 80s. His designs were popular among musicians, artists, and other fashion-forward individuals who appreciated his bold and unconventional aesthetic.
User: I can see why he would have a loyal following. Recently, I met someone who reminded me of this style. They had a very distinctive way of dressing that caught my attention.
Assistant: That sounds intriguing. What was it about their style that caught your eye?
User: Well, they had this Day-Glo-colored jacket that seemed really bold and eye-catching. It was the kind of thing that you couldn't help but notice.
Assistant: That sounds like something Stephen Sprouse might have designed. Did you get a chance to talk to this person and learn more about their fashion sense?
User: Yes, I did. And what I learned was really interesting. This person idolizes Stephen Sprouse and has been collecting his designs for years.
Assistant: That's amazing! It's not every day you meet someone who is so passionate about a particular designer. Did they tell you what it was about Stephen Sprouse's designs that resonated with them?
User: Yes, they did. They told me that they loved the way Stephen Sprouse's designs combined art and fashion, and how his clothing made them feel like they were wearing a piece of art.
Assistant: That's a beautiful sentiment. It's clear that Stephen Sprouse's designs have had a lasting impact on this person, and it's wonderful that they're continuing to celebrate his legacy through their own fashion choices.
User: I completely agree. It was really inspiring to see someone so passionate about fashion and art.
Assistant: It's always exciting to meet someone who shares your interests and passions. And it's even more special when you can learn from them and gain a new appreciation for something, like Stephen Sprouse's designs.
User: Hi, I've been feeling really uninspired by the fashion world lately.
Assistant: Oh, what do you mean by uninspired? Is there something specific that's been bothering you?
User: I don't know, it just feels like everything looks the same. I'm not excited about new trends or styles like I used to be.
Assistant: That's understandable. Fashion trends can be overwhelming and repetitive at times. Have you tried exploring different fashion brands or designers to see if that sparks any interest?
User: Yeah, I've been looking around, but even high-end designers seem to be doing the same thing. It's all just so... formulaic.
Assistant: Formulaic is an interesting word to use. Do you think that's because of the way fashion is presented to consumers, or is it something more fundamental about the industry itself?
User: Hmm, I think it's a bit of both. But I've been noticing that it feels like fashion is more about making money than creating art or expressing oneself.
Assistant: That's a valid concern. The fashion industry is a multi-billion dollar market, after all. Do you think that's changed the way you perceive fashion or your relationship with it?
User: Yeah, it definitely has. I used to love fashion because it was a way for me to express my personality and individuality. But now, it just feels like I'm buying into a commercialized machine.
Assistant: It sounds like you're feeling a bit disconnected from the fashion world. Can you pinpoint when you started feeling this way, or was it a gradual process?
User: Honestly, I think it's been building up over the past few years. But lately, I've come to realize that fashion has become too commercialized, leading to a decrease in my interest and enthusiasm.
Assistant: That makes sense. When an industry becomes overly commercialized, it can be hard to maintain that emotional connection. Do you think there's a way for the fashion industry to balance its commercial side with the creative and artistic aspects that initially drew you in?
User: I'm not sure, but I think it would require a major shift in the way the industry operates. Maybe a greater emphasis on sustainability and supporting smaller, independent designers.
Assistant: Those are great points. Supporting smaller designers and prioritizing sustainability could help create a more diverse and creative fashion landscape. Do you think that would be enough to rekindle your interest in fashion?
User: Yeah, I think it could be a start. I just want to see fashion as a form of self-expression and artistry again, rather than just a way to make a quick profit.
Assistant: I completely understand. Hopefully, the industry will take note of consumers like you who are looking for a more authentic and creative fashion experience.

Assistant: It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed. Have you thought about why your appearance is so important to you?
User: I guess I've always felt like I have to look a certain way to be accepted or respected. It's like I'm trying to prove something to others.

User: You're right. I think I need to focus more on cultivating inner confidence and self-acceptance.

Assistant: Those are great ideas. And remember, if you ever need support or guidance on this journey, I'm here to help.
User: Thank you, Mentor. Your encouragement means a lot to me.
Assistant: Of course, Mentee. We all deserve to feel confident and comfortable in our own skin. And speaking of feeling comfortable, how's your arm and knee doing after that fall a few weeks ago?

Assistant: What do you mean?
User: I don't know, I just feel like I'm not good enough as myself. So I dyed my hair, got some new clothes, and even started wearing glasses.
Assistant: But why? You're perfect just the way you are.
User: I don't feel that way. I see all these other people and they seem so confident and put-together, and I just feel like I'm lacking something.
Assistant: But you have so many great qualities! You're smart, funny, and kind. Plus, your natural hair color looks amazing on you.
User: Thanks, but I just feel like I need to reinvent myself.
Assistant: Have you considered that maybe you're just comparing yourself to others too much? It's great to have role models, but you don't need to completely change yourself to be like them.
User: I guess you're right. It's just hard sometimes.
Assistant: I understand. But remember, you're unique and special just the way you are. You don't need to be anyone else to be amazing.
User: Hey, have you seen the art piece I made last weekend?
Assistant: No, I haven't. What did you make?
User: It's a blue background with a white circle in the middle. And the circle has a black dot in the center. I was going for a minimalist vibe.
Assistant: Oh, that sounds interesting. Did you paint it or use some other medium?
User: I used acrylic paints. I find it very relaxing to paint on my days off.
Assistant: That's cool. I've always admired people who can create visual art. I'm more of a writer myself.
User: I know what you mean. I used to write in high school, but I've been more into visual art lately.
Assistant: Speaking of high school, do you remember the time when we had to fix that table in the student lounge because it was broken?
User: Oh yeah, I remember that. I was always good with tools, so I took the lead on that project.
Assistant: It's great to have those skills. Loyalty is also an important quality, like when you turned down that job offer to stay with our company.
User: Definitely. I couldn't imagine betraying the trust that the company has placed in me. Speaking of trust, I sometimes feel like I'm being controlled by society's social rules.
Assistant: Yeah, it can be tough to balance your own expression with what's expected of you. But at the same time, it's important to respect certain societal norms.
User: I agree with that. And speaking of unfair situations, I released Hunter from the ropes because I knew he was innocent and didn't deserve to be punished.
Assistant: Wow, that was very brave of you. I hope everything turned out okay for him.
User: It did. He was able to clear his name and I'm glad I could help. But anyways, back to the art piece I made, if you want to see it, I could bring it in tomorrow.
Assistant: Sure, I'd love to see it! Visual art always fascinates me.

User: How has Nicolas Ghesquière incorporated the LV monogram into his collections, and what are some of his most creative uses of the design?: It was 1854 when Louis Vuitton established his luggage business in Paris at 4 Rue Neuve des Capucines. As rail and then automobile travel became an established part of life, Vuitton’s business began to grow. Carried by the likes of Paul Poiret, Dora Maar, and Francis Picabia, LV luggage was not only a status symbol but also a practical purchase: Its trunks were—and still are—waterproof to prevent accidental damage to the items inside. They first appeared in the LV monogram pattern in 1896.
On August 4th, Louis Vuitton, the founder of one of the world’s leading luxury brands, would have turned 195 years old. Even if you don’t know the story of Monsieur Vuitton, you know his monogram. You may recognize it from Nicolas Ghesquière’s runway collections (or Marc Jacobs’s before him), from Takashi Murakami’s Pop-minded collaboration of 2003, from Catherine Deneuve’s traveling trunks, or from Dapper Dan’s boutique on East 125th Street in Harlem. How you know the monogram isn’t what matters—it’s that you know it. The interlocking L and V with floral pattern was designed by Louis Vuitton’s son, Georges Vuitton, in 1896 as a way to brand his nascent box and luggage business, and in the 120 years since, it’s become one of the most recognizable marks in the world.
Within the fashion arena, the LV monogram is having something of a resurgence. Since Ghesquière was named artistic director in 2013, the designer has made a point of incorporating it into his collections in new and novel ways—see: the floral-shaped heels of his Spring 2015 boots. Celebrate the history of the iconic house with this look back at its logo in 15 bite-size notes.
As daywear became a growing category for women in the ’60s and ’70s, so did handbags for Louis Vuitton. From the Speedy style now popular again to the bucket, seen here on a ’72 episode of Bewitched, an LV purse became a coveted item among modern women.
Right: In 1997, Marc Jacobs—then an on-the-rise New York designer who had been fired from Perry Ellis several years earlier—was named creative director at Louis Vuitton. Jacobs’s appointment gave new life to the monogram, making the house’s staid hatboxes and new Monogram Vernis collection popular among Jacobs’s model friends like Naomi Campbell and Kate Moss.
Jacobs loves to push boundaries, and after much convincing, he convinced the company to allow Stephen Sprouse to create a graffiti version of Vuitton’s monogram. “Louis Vuitton” and “LV” were painted over the house’s traditional brown-on-brown print—the first time its monogram had ever been updated—and the bags became pop culture sensations. For Jacobs’s final collection for Vuitton, he resurrected the Sprouse design as body paint on model Edie Campbell.
In 2003, Jacobs introduced another monogram collaboration with Japanese artist Takashi Murakami. Murakami remade the monogram in white with multicolored logos and characters and in pink with cherry blossom designs for his first series. In 2004 and 2005 he added an actual cherry print and denim. It was immortalized as the must-have bag for teens and 20-somethings when it appeared on the arm of the poisonously popular Regina George in Tina Fey’s hit Mean Girls in 2004.
Throughout the rest of Jacobs’s tenure at Louis Vuitton, he continued to rework and update the house’s monogram bags. Spring 2007 saw an all-denim, Frankenstein-ed bag made from stitching together other pre-existing LV styles; Spring 2010, ombré-dyed messenger bags; and Fall 2010, sequin embellishments.
As the monogram grew in popularity, so did the range of monogrammed products. On the runway, Jacobs used it for hats, tights, umbrellas, fans, and fur muffs, select versions of which were available at retail.
Artist Richard Prince collaborated with the brand for Spring 2008, creating jewel-toned bags painted with his irreverent artworks. That season’s show was opened by a series of supermodels dressed as nurses from his “Nurse Paintings” series. The idea caught on on the streets too, where Ulyana Sergeenko wore a full LV nurse ensemble in Paris.
The monogram has also inspired its fare share of artists, including Sylvie Fleury, who crafted a bronze sculpture of the signature LV duffel in 2001. Murakami has also incorporated the monogram into his Pop works following his collaboration with the brand.
Nicolas Ghesquière’s first Louis Vuitton collection revitalized Paris Fashion Week with its wearable silhouettes and vaguely ’70s spirit. Key to the collection’s impact was Vuitton’s new Petite Malle bag, styled after its iconic trunks. Outside the Spring 2015 shows, it was the bag of choice from New York to Paris.
Ghesquière’s other experiments with the monogram have ranged from twisting it into an undulating pattern on handbags (Fall 2014) to carving boot heels in the design’s four-petaled flower shape (Spring 2015). For Resort 2016, it appeared on ready-to-wear, when leather dresses were perforated with the floral pattern.
Left: For the 160th anniversary of Louis Vuitton’s founding, the house commissioned six designers and artists to design bags in its classic monogram colors. Karl Lagerfeld, Frank Gehry, Cindy Sherman, Marc Newson, Christian Louboutin, and Rei Kawakubo participated, each creating a version of the purse with some of their signature flair—Kawakubo’s featured giant bean-shaped holes, while Gehry’s was a twisted box. The most fun was Lagerfeld’s contribution: a punching bag with matching monogrammed boxing gloves. A statement on the decades-old accessories race between LV and Chanel, perhaps?
Right: With Jonathan Anderson at Loewe and Jeremy Scott at Moschino, Ghesquière has helped make branded wares the look of the moment.

User: How did the makeup at Marni's fall show incorporate a 1940s styling?
Generate according to: Plum, prune, bordeaux, black cherry—there are many ways to describe the dark, reddish-purple lip color we've seen over and over again on the Milan runways. But whatever you decide to call it, if you're going to try out this moody lipstick trend, there's an initial step that you absolutely don't want to forget.
Inspired by Hitchcock's black-and-white thriller Rebecca, the hair and makeup at Marni's fall show had a distinctive '40s bent, albeit with a twist. The classic pin-curl set stopped at the crown, where the hair then evolved into a soft, bed-head-like texture. And instead of opting for the traditional shade of red, makeup artist Tom Pecheux chose an intense maroon lip color that he created by painting on a layer of M.A.C. Blind Score Casual Color followed by M.A.C. Night Moth Lip Pencil.
But the most important step when applying dark lipstick starts before you lay down any pigment. "The minute the models arrive backstage, we apply a thick layer of lip balm," said Pecheux, who then prepped the skin, applied concealer and highlighter, and groomed the brows, leaving the lips until the very end. Once the rest of the face was complete, Pecheux blotted off any residual balm off the lips before painting on the cream and drawing on the pencil. It's an easy step that may seem slightly throwaway, but it makes all the difference, taking a subversive shade like this from goth to total glamour.

1. Bright, bold eyeshadow - Several designers showcased models with colorful eyeshadow in shades like electric blue, vivid green, and bright purple.

2. Graphic eyeliner - Graphic eyeliner was a popular trend in Milan, with many designers showcasing models with bold, dramatic liner in graphic shapes like triangles and squares.

3. Blush overload - Many designers opted for an exaggerated blush look, with models sporting bright, rosy cheeks that extended up to the temples.

4. Natural, glowing skin - While there were plenty of bold makeup looks on the runways, many designers also embraced minimal, natural-looking makeup with glowing, radiant skin as the focus.

User: Can you tell me more about the "blush overload" trend? How can I achieve that look without making it look too overpowering?
Assistant: Sure, the "blush overload" trend involves applying an exaggerated amount of blush that extends up towards the temples, creating a flushed, youthful appearance. If you'd like to achieve this look without making it look too overpowering, there are a few strategies you can try:

1. Choose the right shade of blush - Pick a color that complements your skin tone and looks natural on you. If you're fair-skinned, a light pink or peachy shade will work well. For medium or deeper skin tones, try a warm, golden hue or a deeper rose color.

2. Use a light hand - Start with a small amount of blush on your brush or fingertips, and gradually build up the color if you feel you need more. Remember, it's easier to add more than it is to remove excess product.

3. Blend well - Be sure to blend your blush thoroughly, so that there are no harsh lines or streaks. Using a fluffy, domed brush will help you achieve a more diffuse, natural-looking finish.

4. Use the right placement - Focus the majority of your blush on the apples of your cheeks, and then blend it upward and outward towards your temples. Stop just below your eyes, so that the blush doesn't extend too far up your face.

By using these tips, you can get a bold, rosy look that feels fresh and youthful, without looking clownish or overdone.
User: How did the fashion design students at O'More College of Design help fill the need for plus-size prom dresses? Answer according to: Fashion design schools are notorious for extravagant fashion shows, showcasing their student’s latest and greatest designs.
Many fashion design schools require an end-of-term catwalk event for course credits, but few take an off-the-cuff opportunity to do something unique.
As a local television network reported earlier in December, a Nashville, TN fashion design school decided to work on a unique project and give back to needy teens in their community.
Beth Glascock has been collecting prom dresses for needy teenagers for a while now and collected nearly two-thousand in the past couple of years. Glascock is the master mind behind The Fairy Godmother Project, a local non-profit cause that began in 2010 as a group of 5 friends decided to create the organization as a New Year’s Resolution.
The project is aimed at offering the area’s teens that might otherwise be unable to afford prom wear, the opportunity to shine at their school’s formal dance. The Fairy Godmother Project, co-founded by Merideth Cooper, Amy Doyle, Heather Skaar, and Laura Zimmerman turned to the students at the fashion school to help meet their latest challenge.
Plus-size dresses have always been hard to come by for the group and this year was no exception. They simply had too few plus sized dresses in the collection to meet the needs of the community. This is where the students of the fashion design school at O’More College of Design stepped in to fill the need.
In a period of only fifteen hours, senior fashion design student Christa Allison and some other students created new plus-size dresses using some of The Fairy Godmother Project’s other formal wear.
“This is a very under-served size group, and it is so great to have a group of young people to create these dresses for them,” Laura Zimmerman said according to O’More’s blog.

User: Hello, I hope you're doing well. I recently read "Motherless Brooklyn" and I didn't enjoy it. There is no doubt in my mind that Jonathan Lethem is a gifted writer. His prose is crisp, a little crazy, and often a lot of fun to read. I was intrigued by his idea of a detective with Tourette's syndrome, which makes him compulsive (actually, a fairly useful trait for a detective) and also given to quirky flights of language. The reviews of the book led me to expect something with the page-turning qualities of a good murder mystery combined with an unusual, and more poetic, use of language than you generally find in genre fiction. The book seemed to live up to that description for the first fifty pages or so, but I seriously question whether many reviewers read the entire novel, because by the middle the plot bogs down, it becomes clear that the characters are never going to develop into anything more complicated than you'd find in a B movie, and the language, at first intriguing, becomes just plain eccentric. Lethem has talent, but he wasted it on this novel.
Assistant: I understand your disappointment with "Motherless Brooklyn". Having lived in Brooklyn for a little more than 2 decades -- and spent most of my life in the greater met area -- there is little that rings "True". Because this is a story - not a non-fiction re-telling. And yet it does have elements of both. So it's not exactly a guide to a time or place. But a wonderful re-imagining of both.
